Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session of Day 1. The Afghanistan players are out in the middle. Kevin Kasuza and Prince Masvaure will open the innings for Zimbabwe. Yamin Ahmadzai will start the proceedings for Afghanistan.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

So Afghanistan have disappointed with the bat but can they make amends with the ball now? It is a good wicket for the bowlers as there is something on offer for the pacers and some turn for the spinners as well. Zimbabwe will look to ensure they will finish the day strongly and get a firm grip of the game. Can the Zimbabwe openers see off the new ball threat? Join us for the final session to find out.

Smiles all-around the Zimbabwe players and they will be very happy with how things have panned out so far. They were brilliant with the ball. Blessing Muzarabani gave them the ideal start and set the ball rolling. His opening bowling partner, Victor Nyauchi too joined the act. The pair shouldered the responsibility and ensured to hunt down Afghanistan's top order. Muzarabani was the star picking up 4 while Nyauchi finished with 3. Tiripano, Raza, and Sean Williams shared the three wickets amongst themselves.

After opting to bat, Afghanistan's innings never got going. They lost wicket off the first ball of the game and that set the tone for the innings. Apart from Ibrahim Zadran's 31 and Afsar Zazai's 37, there was hardly anything to write about. When a team loses 5 wickets in the first session it is always a herculean task to put a fight with the bat. That is what happened here and the hosts crumbled with the bat. Poor performance with the willow by the Asian side and they will be gutted with their performance.

Brilliant bowling display from Zimbabwe. Having put to bowl, they have done the job and ensured that they bundle out the hosts for a paltry total in the first innings. A very disappointing effort with the bat from Afghanistan. They will be gutted with the display they put on after opting to bat. This will also be TEA ON DAY 1!

So the first session clearly belonged to Zimbabwe but Afghanistan still have their skipper out in the middle. Can Asghar Afghan and Afsar Zazai pull things in their sides' favor in the second session or will Zimbabwe continue their domination in the second session as well? Join us for the post-Lunch session to find out.

Delightful session for Zimbabwe! They will be very happy with how things have panned out in the first session of this Test. Barring the over rate, everything else has gone according to the plan for the visitors. Blessing Muzarabani set the tone with a wicket of the first ball and followed that with another scalp. Victor Nyauchi joined the act and ended the session with 3 wickets. The two pacers bowled the majority of the overs in this session. Tiripano and Burl bowled 4 and 1 overs respectively but have not tasted success yet.

After winning the toss and opting to bat, Afghanistan would have looked for a steady start but what they got was completely the opposite of that. They lost Abdul Malik in the very first ball of the game and found themselves behind from that moment on. Apart from Ibrahim Zadran, there was hardly anything from the batters. They still have their experienced skipper, Asghar Afghan and Afsar Zazai out in the middle. The onus will be on these two to take their side out of troubled waters.

An excellent session for Zimbabwe. They have dominated this session and the pie of the session will belong to the red of Afghanistan. The hosts have been subpar in the first session and will be disappointed with their effort so far. A lot of players got starts but were unable to kick on from there and that has hurt the hosts badly.

OUT! BOWLED! What a start for Blessing Muzarabani and Zimbabwe. They have started this Test with a bang! A wicket off the very first ball. Swing, bounce, and the sound of timber. That is how Blessing has got the tourists going. Blessing Muzarabani bowls a good length ball pitching outside off and makes the ball jag back in a lot. Abdul Malik looks to defend but the ball bounces a tad more than he expected. It hits the higher portion of Malik's bat and comes down to hit the stumps. Perfect start for Zimbabwe but a terrible one for Afghanistan!
Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Abdul Malik, Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi, Asghar Afghan (C), Afsar Zazai (WK), Munir Ahmad, Amir Hamza, Yamin Ahmadzai, Zahir Khan, Abdul Wasi.

Done and dusted with the national anthems and we are all set for the action to begin! The Zimbabwe players are in a huddle before they take their respective positions in the field. Abdul Malik and Ibrahim Zadran stride out to open the innings for Afghanistan. Blessing Muzarabani is all set to operate with the new ball first up.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Kevin Kasuza, Prince Masvaure, Sean Williams (C), Wesley Madhevere, Tarisai Musakanda, Sikandar Raza, Ryan Burl, Regis Chakabva (WK), Donald Tiripano, Blessing Muzarabani, Victor Nyauchi.

Both sides have made their way out to the middle for their respective national anthems. First up it will be the away side, Zimbabwe's followed by Afghanistan. We are not far away from the start of action!

Zimbabwe head coach, Lalchand Rajput is caught for a chat. Lalchand Rajput says they have had good preparations. Tells the batters have got runs and the bowlers have got time in the middle. Tells Test cricket is about patience. Rajput says that they will miss the senior guys but adds this is a good platform for the young guys. Tells it is difficult to fill those shoes. Lalchand says getting big scores is important.

Afghanistan coach, Lance Klusner is caught for a chat. Lance Klusner says it is a privilege to coach this exciting side. Tells that they have tried to have fun in the bio-bubble but admits it has been tough. Adds that if they can win the mental battle in the bio-bubble they will be in a good space. Klusner says that they will not make excuses of having not played for a year.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is the pitch analyst for the day. Mawoyo tells there is lot of grass and feels very green. Tells the surface is very dry and seamers will be able to extract moment. Tells the other side is very different as it is very dry. Adds there will be something there for the seamers and spinners.
TOSS - It is time for the spin of the coin. Afghanistan win the toss and elect to bat!

Hello and welcome to the first of the 2-match Test series between Afghanistan and Zimbabwe. Both sides are playing red-ball cricket after a long time and both will be eager to get a win in the longest format. Zimbabwe will be eager to show the world that they are still a side that can be dangerous on their day and with a win here they will look to put out a statement. Afghanistan, on the other hand, will look to continue their progress in the longest format with a win. A win here will see them take a step forward in the right direction. Can Zimbabwe upset the Asian side or will Asghar Afghan's men continue their progress? Stay tuned for toss and further updates.
